exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 1L backbone (IFL/FOLFIRI + bevacizumab) whose mechanism (VEGF-A neutralization) does not target the patient's nominated targetable features (KRAS A59T, PIK3CA M1043I, APC E1295, TP53 R273, SMAD4 R361H, BCL2L1/TOP1 amp). Libby is feature-targeting scope only; SoC backbones run through the treating team independent of this dossier.
intervention_label: Bevacizumab + IFL (AVF2107g)
notes: Anchor RCT for the bevacizumab-plus-chemo backbone in 1L mCRC (mOS 20.3 vs 15.6 mo, HR 0.66, p<0.001). Listed for audit trail; not part of Libby's feature-targeting synthesis.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 1L backbone (FOLFOX/XELOX + bevacizumab). Mechanism does not target the patient's nominated features.
intervention_label: Bevacizumab + FOLFOX-4 or XELOX (NO16966)
notes: 1L oxaliplatin + bev RCT (mPFS 9.4 vs 8.0 mo, HR 0.83). Backbone evidence retained in the audit trail.

exclusion_reason: Backbone chemotherapy comparison (FOLFIRI vs mIFL vs CapeIRI) — mechanism does not target the patient's nominated features.
intervention_label: FOLFIRI vs mIFL vs CapeIRI (BICC-C)
notes: Established FOLFIRI as the favored 1L irinotecan-fluoropyrimidine schedule (mOS 23.1 mo vs 17.6/18.9 mo). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: FIRE-3 cetuximab vs bevacizumab in RAS-WT 1L mCRC — the patient has KRAS A59T (atypical RAS-mutated), so the RAS-WT subset that drives the survival signal does not include them. Both arms are SoC backbones not targeting the patient's specific features. Atypical-KRAS / anti-EGFR question is covered separately in Bucket H rows.
intervention_label: FOLFIRI + cetuximab vs FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (FIRE-3)
notes: RAS-WT 1L mCRC: cetuximab arm mOS 28.7 vs 25.0 mo, HR 0.77. Anchor for the cetuximab-vs-bev comparison; KRAS A59T patient is not RAS-WT by current consensus.

exclusion_reason: Intensive triplet chemo + bev (FOLFOXIRI-bev) is a backbone-intensification option — mechanism does not target the patient's nominated targetable features. Worth surfacing to the treating team as a 1L alternative; Libby does not rank it.
intervention_label: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (TRIBE)
notes: Intensive triplet improved mPFS (12.1 vs 9.7 mo, HR 0.75) and mOS in updated analysis (29.8 vs 25.8 mo, HR 0.80). Relevant if treating team considers re-induction in young ECOG-1 patient.

exclusion_reason: Backbone sequencing trial (FOLFOXIRI-bev upfront + reintroduction vs sequential FOLFOX-bev then FOLFIRI-bev). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Upfront FOLFOXIRI + bev (TRIBE2)
notes: Strategy trial — upfront triplet improved mPFS2 (19.2 vs 16.4 mo, HR 0.74) and mOS (27.4 vs 22.5 mo, HR 0.82). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Maintenance backbone after induction CAPOX-bev. Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Capecitabine + bevacizumab maintenance (CAIRO3)
notes: Maintenance arm improved PFS1 (11.7 vs 8.5 mo) over observation. Decision-relevant for post-HIPEC maintenance strategy; audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Backbone comparison (FOLFIRI-bev vs FOLFOX-bev stratified by ERCC1). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: mFOLFOX6-bev vs FOLFIRI-bev (MAVERICC, biomarker-stratified)
notes: Phase 2 biomarker-stratified RCT: PFS/OS comparable between arms; numeric trend favored FOLFIRI-bev. Anchors the 1L FOLFIRI-bev choice the patient is already on.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 2L backbone (aflibercept + FOLFIRI). Anti-angiogenic mechanism does not target the patient's nominated features.
intervention_label: Aflibercept + FOLFIRI (VELOUR, 2L)
notes: 2L after oxaliplatin failure: mOS 13.5 vs 12.1 mo (HR 0.82, p=0.003). Anchors aflibercept; only relevant if sequence switches to FOLFOX 1L.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 2L backbone (ramucirumab + FOLFIRI). Anti-VEGFR2 mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Ramucirumab + FOLFIRI (RAISE, 2L post-bev)
notes: 2L after bev-containing 1L: mOS 13.3 vs 11.7 mo (HR 0.84, p=0.02). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 3L backbone (regorafenib monotherapy). Multikinase VEGFR/TIE2 mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Regorafenib monotherapy (CORRECT, 3L+)
notes: Pivotal: mOS 6.4 vs 5.0 mo (HR 0.77, p=0.0052). High G3+ AE rate (hand-foot 17%, fatigue 10%, HTN 7%). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Regorafenib backbone confirmation in Asian patients (CONCUR). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Regorafenib monotherapy (CONCUR, Asian cohort, 3L+)
notes: mOS 8.8 vs 6.3 mo (HR 0.55, p=0.00016). Replicates CORRECT in Asian population.

exclusion_reason: Regorafenib dose-optimization (ReDOS, 80→160 mg ramp). Mechanism does not target the patient's features; useful tolerance-management evidence for the treating team.
intervention_label: Regorafenib dose-escalation (ReDOS, 80→120→160 mg)
notes: Ramp-up dosing matched the standard 160 mg arm on activity with lower G3 AE incidence (hand-foot, fatigue, HTN, diarrhea). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 3L backbone (TAS-102 monotherapy). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) monotherapy (RECOURSE, 3L+)
notes: Pivotal: mOS 7.1 vs 5.3 mo (HR 0.68, p<0.001). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 3L backbone (TAS-102 + bev). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Trifluridine/tipiracil + bevacizumab (SUNLIGHT, 3L)
notes: Pivotal RCT: mOS 10.8 vs 7.5 mo (HR 0.61, p<0.001). Establishes TAS-102 + bev as 3L SoC. Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 3L backbone (fruquintinib). Anti-VEGFR1/2/3 mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Fruquintinib (FRESCO, Chinese 3L+)
notes: Chinese pivotal: mOS 9.3 vs 6.6 mo (HR 0.65). Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Standard-of-care 3L backbone (fruquintinib, global confirmatory). Mechanism does not target the patient's features.
intervention_label: Fruquintinib (FRESCO-2, global 3L+)
notes: Global confirmatory: mOS 7.4 vs 4.8 mo (HR 0.66). Drove US approval Nov 2023. Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: Surgical / locoregional intervention (CRS-HIPEC vs CRS alone). Not a feature-targeting drug. Surfaced separately as a critical sequencing context for the planned HIPEC window; the treating team owns this decision.
intervention_label: Oxaliplatin HIPEC + CRS vs CRS alone (PRODIGE 7)
notes: Critical negative trial: oxaliplatin HIPEC added to CRS did NOT improve OS (41.7 vs 41.2 mo) or RFS (13.1 vs 11.1 mo) in CRC peritoneal metastases, with higher 60-day morbidity in the HIPEC arm. CRS retains the OS signal; HIPEC does not. This is the central caveat to flag for the patient's planned peri-operative HIPEC window.

exclusion_reason: Adjuvant oxaliplatin HIPEC after primary resection for high-risk T4/perforated colon cancer. Surgical locoregional intervention; not a feature-targeting drug.
intervention_label: Adjuvant oxaliplatin HIPEC for T4/perforated colon cancer (COLOPEC)
notes: Adjuvant HIPEC did NOT improve 18-mo peritoneal-disease-free survival (80.9% vs 76.2%). Together with PRODIGE 7 and PROPHYLOCHIP, completes the negative HIPEC trifecta in colon cancer.

exclusion_reason: Second-look surgery + HIPEC for patients at high risk of peritoneal recurrence (PROPHYLOCHIP/PRODIGE 15). Surgical intervention; not feature-targeting.
intervention_label: Second-look surgery + HIPEC vs surveillance (PROPHYLOCHIP-PRODIGE 15)
notes: 3-yr DFS 44% vs 53% (HR 0.97, p=0.82). No benefit from prophylactic second-look + HIPEC. Audit-trail row reinforcing HIPEC skepticism for the planned window.

exclusion_reason: Perioperative systemic chemo (FOLFOX/CAPOX/FOLFIRI ± bev) around CRS-HIPEC. Backbone chemo + bev; mechanism does not target the patient's features. Relevant as the sequencing-with-HIPEC trial for the patient's window.
intervention_label: Perioperative systemic chemo + CRS-HIPEC vs CRS-HIPEC alone (CAIRO6)
notes: Phase 2/3 perioperative therapy improved PFS/DFS but not OS over CRS-HIPEC alone in resectable CPM; safety acceptable. Decision-relevant for the patient's planned HIPEC pathway. Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: PIPAC monotherapy in unresectable CPM. Locoregional drug delivery, not feature-targeted. Mechanism rationale (oxaliplatin via aerosol) does not address KRAS A59T, PIK3CA M1043I, or other features. Audit-trail row.
intervention_label: Oxaliplatin PIPAC (CRC-PIPAC, unresectable CPM)
notes: Phase 2 single-arm, n=20: mPFS 3.5 mo, mOS 8.0 mo, 15% major AE rate. Decision-relevant if upfront CRS-HIPEC is deferred (trial row NCT04329494 maps to City of Hope PIPAC platform).

exclusion_reason: MOUNTAINEER tucatinib + trastuzumab in HER2+ RAS-WT mCRC. Patient has KRAS A59T (atypical RAS-mutated), so the RAS-WT label criterion fails on protocol text — even if HER2 returns amplified on pending NGS, MOUNTAINEER-label use is not gated open. HER2 is not among the patient's nominated targetable features at intake.
intervention_label: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER, HER2+ RAS-WT mCRC)
notes: ORR 38%, mDoR 12.4 mo, mPFS 8.2 mo, mOS 24.1 mo. FDA accelerated approval Jan 2023. Audit-trail row; patient's KRAS A59T blocks the RAS-WT label gate.

exclusion_reason: MOUNTAINEER final analysis. Same RAS-WT exclusion as primary publication.
intervention_label: Tucatinib + trastuzumab (MOUNTAINEER final analysis)
notes: Final OS analysis — durable benefit in RAS-WT HER2+ refractory mCRC. KRAS A59T patient remains excluded by label.

exclusion_reason: HER2+ ADC (T-DXd). HER2 is NOT among the patient's nominated targetable features; HER2 status is not reported on profile.json. Out of Libby's feature scope until/unless HER2 amp returns on pending NGS.
intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-CRC01, HER2-expressing mCRC)
notes: Cohort A (HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+/ISH+): ORR 45.3%, mPFS 6.9 mo. Cross-tumor / cross-biomarker reference. Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: HER2+ ADC, including RAS-mutant patients (unlike MOUNTAINEER). HER2 is not among the patient's nominated features; pending NGS would gate eligibility. Out of Libby scope at intake.
intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-CRC02, HER2+ mCRC, 5.4 vs 6.4 mg/kg)
notes: ORR 38% (5.4 mg/kg arm), mPFS 5.8 mo, mOS ~16 mo. RAS-mutant subset allowed, including KRAS-mutated patients — would become highly relevant if HER2 returns amplified on pending NGS. ILD ~8% (5.4 mg/kg).

exclusion_reason: Trastuzumab + lapatinib in HER2+ KRAS exon 2 WT mCRC. Patient's KRAS A59T (exon 3) was outside HERACLES eligibility, and HER2 is not on the patient's nominated targetable features. Audit-trail row for HER2 landscape.
intervention_label: Trastuzumab + lapatinib (HERACLES, HER2+ KRAS-WT mCRC)
notes: ORR 30%, mPFS 5.2 mo, mOS 11.5 mo. Original HER2-dual-blockade proof-of-concept in CRC.

exclusion_reason: Sotorasib + panitumumab in KRAS G12C mCRC. Sotorasib is a G12C-specific covalent inhibitor binding the switch-II cysteine that KRAS A59T does not provide. The drug does not target A59T in any plausible mechanistic sense.
intervention_label: Sotorasib + panitumumab (CodeBreaK 300, KRAS G12C mCRC)
notes: 960 mg arm: ORR 26%, mPFS 5.6 vs 2.2 mo SoC (HR 0.49). Anchor for the KRAS-G12C therapy class — patient's A59T is NOT a covered allele for any approved KRAS-targeted drug. Critical caveat to surface to the patient and family.

exclusion_reason: Adagrasib ± cetuximab in KRAS G12C mCRC. KRAS A59T lacks the switch-II cysteine that the G12C covalent inhibitor needs. Not in mechanism scope for A59T.
intervention_label: Adagrasib ± cetuximab (KRYSTAL-1, KRAS G12C mCRC)
notes: Monotherapy ORR 19%; adagrasib + cetuximab ORR 46%, mDoR 7.6 mo. Drove FDA accelerated approval of the combination (Jun 2024) in G12C mCRC. A59T patient is not eligible.

exclusion_reason: CodeBreaK 300 OS update — same KRAS G12C-only eligibility as primary publication. Not in mechanism scope for KRAS A59T.
intervention_label: Sotorasib + panitumumab OS update (CodeBreaK 300)
notes: OS update favored sotorasib 960 mg arm numerically. Audit-trail row.

exclusion_reason: CodeBreaK 101 expansion — sotorasib + pembrolizumab / atezolizumab. KRAS G12C-only eligibility.
intervention_label: Sotorasib + ICI combinations (CodeBreaK 101)
notes: Sotorasib + ICI mainly NSCLC. Audit-trail row only — A59T not eligible.

exclusion_reason: KRYSTAL-7 adagrasib + pembrolizumab in KRAS G12C NSCLC. G12C-only; A59T patient is not eligible by allele or by tumor type.
intervention_label: Adagrasib + pembrolizumab (KRYSTAL-7, KRAS G12C NSCLC)
notes: KRAS G12C NSCLC; not CRC and not A59T-relevant.

intervention_label: Panitumumab + FOLFIRI in KRAS A59T mCRC (case report)
intervention_dose: Panitumumab 6 mg/kg IV Q2W + FOLFIRI
indication: Metastatic colon cancer harboring KRAS A59T
population_detail: Single patient with KRAS A59T (initially read as KRAS exon-2 WT on limited testing; A59T disclosed on broader NGS after FOLFIRI-bev progression). Switched to panitumumab + FOLFIRI on disease progression.
outcome: Radiographic PR (~36% reduction) with concurrent CEA decline; SD continued.
variance_or_ci: single patient — descriptive only
median_dor_or_pfs: 8 months on panitumumab + FOLFIRI before subsequent progression

outcomes.name: RR
outcomes.notes: single-patient PR with -36% target-lesion change and CEA decline

outcomes.name: DoR
outcomes.notes: panitumumab + FOLFIRI response duration before progression

safety_summary: No new safety signals; standard panitumumab + FOLFIRI tolerance.
notes: Decision-relevant precedent — challenges blanket assumption that all atypical KRAS mutations confer anti-EGFR resistance. A single PR in a 37yo with A59T is hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory; balance against Sorich/Schirripa meta-analytic signal that non-canonical RAS mutations attenuate anti-EGFR benefit. PMC6295659. AE detail not captured beyond 'no new safety signals' — abstract-only in PMC, no AE table.

intervention_label: Anti-EGFR mAbs in extended-RAS-mutant mCRC (meta-analysis)
intervention_dose: Pooled cetuximab- and panitumumab-containing regimens across 9 RCTs
indication: Metastatic colorectal cancer stratified by extended-RAS status (KRAS exons 2/3/4 and NRAS exons 2/3/4)
population_detail: Pooled across CRYSTAL, PRIME, OPUS, FIRE-3, PEAK, 20020408, 20050181, NORDIC-VII, MRC COIN — 5,948 patients; ~20% of KRAS exon-2 WT tumors carried a 'new RAS' alteration.
design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
outcome: OS / PFS hazard ratios for anti-EGFR therapy by extended-RAS status
variance_or_ci: 95% CI 0.91-1.28 (OS in new-RAS-mut subset); PFS HR 1.03 (0.78-1.36)

outcomes.name: HR_PFS
outcomes.notes: PFS benefit confined to all-RAS WT

safety_summary: Class-typical anti-EGFR rash and hypomagnesemia plus chemo toxicity; safety was not the focus of this meta-analysis.
notes: Foundational evidence that non-canonical RAS mutations (which include codon 59) abrogate the anti-EGFR survival benefit at the population level. The Lochhead A59T case report sits against this signal, not with it.

intervention_label: NRAS / atypical RAS mutations as anti-EGFR resistance markers (retrospective cohort)
intervention_dose: Cetuximab- and panitumumab-containing regimens, retrospective
indication: Metastatic colorectal cancer, chemo-refractory
population_detail: n=786 mCRC patients; NRAS mutated in 47 (6%). NRAS-mut vs KRAS-mut groups compared for clinicopathology and anti-EGFR response.
outcome: Median OS and anti-EGFR response rate by RAS status
variance_or_ci: 0/9 evaluable NRAS-mut patients responded to anti-EGFR
safety_summary: Retrospective; safety not assessed as a primary endpoint.
notes: Adjacent biology — extends the 'atypical-RAS-blocks-anti-EGFR' signal to NRAS. The patient's KRAS A59T sits in the same conceptual family. Reinforces the Sorich meta-analytic call.

intervention_label: Functional / clinical characterization of atypical KRAS/NRAS mutations in mCRC
intervention_dose: Cetuximab- and panitumumab-containing regimens, retrospective
indication: Metastatic colorectal cancer with atypical (non-G12/G13/Q61) KRAS or NRAS mutations
population_detail: Cohort of mCRC patients with atypical KRAS/NRAS alterations — A59, K117, A146, others — profiled functionally and clinically; subset received anti-EGFR therapy.
comparator: Canonical KRAS-mut (G12/G13/Q61) and all-RAS WT comparators
outcome: Anti-EGFR response rate and PFS in atypical-KRAS subset
variance_or_ci: A146/A59 alleles show partial residual sensitivity in some cases; functional assays show weaker MAPK output than G12 mutants

outcomes.name: RR
outcomes.notes: occasional responders observed; lower MAPK signal than G12/G13

safety_summary: Not assessed.
notes: Most directly relevant atypical-KRAS / anti-EGFR paper for the case — functional and clinical heterogeneity at A59 and adjacent codons. PMC8364867. Supports the position that A59T should be assessed individually rather than treated as a flat anti-EGFR contraindication.

intervention_label: Immuno-oncology biomarker enrichment in KRAS A59T tumors
intervention_dose: Observational biomarker analysis (no intervention)
indication: Solid tumors (colorectal predominant) harboring KRAS A59T
population_detail: Caris real-world cohort: KRAS A59T variant cases compared to KRAS WT and other KRAS mutants for PD-L1, TMB, MSI, and immune-microenvironment markers.
comparator: Other KRAS alleles and KRAS-WT comparator
outcome: Enrichment of immuno-oncology biomarkers in A59T tumors
variance_or_ci: PD-L1 + TMB higher in A59T-mut vs other KRAS-mut CRC

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: A59T tumors enriched for IO biomarkers vs other KRAS alleles

safety_summary: Not applicable (observational).
notes: The patient is MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg by intake — the opposite of the A59T-enriched pattern described here. The A59T immuno-oncology hypothesis does not light up for this individual. Worth surfacing so the board knows the IO-enrichment signal exists at the allele level but doesn't apply here. PMC8224072.

intervention_label: Alpelisib (BYL719) monotherapy in PIK3CA-altered solid tumors (first-in-human)
intervention_dose: Alpelisib 400 mg PO QD or 150 mg PO BID (MTD)
indication: Advanced solid tumors with PIK3CA alterations (mixed: breast, CRC, gynecologic, endometrial)
population_detail: n=134 PIK3CA-altered solid tumors; CRC subset included. PIK3CA mutations spanned the canonical helical / kinase hotspots (E542K, E545K, H1047R) and rarer alleles.
outcome: ORR and clinical activity across tumor types
variance_or_ci: 8/134 PRs total (1 breast, 2 CRC, 4 gyn/endometrial, 1 other)
safety_summary: Hyperglycemia, rash, GI toxicity (nausea/diarrhea) class-typical for PI3K-alpha inhibition. G3+ hyperglycemia ~20%, G3+ rash ~10%.
notes: Anchor for alpelisib's PIK3CA-mutant pharmacology in solid tumors — including the 2 CRC responders. Closest standalone CRC + PIK3CA-targeting clinical readout outside breast cancer.

intervention_label: Inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant (INAVO120, HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mut breast cancer)
intervention_dose: Inavolisib 9 mg PO QD + palbociclib 125 mg PO QD (3 weeks on / 1 off) + fulvestrant 500 mg IM Q4W
indication: HR+/HER2- PIK3CA-mutated metastatic breast cancer (1L after endocrine therapy)
population_detail: n=325 with PIK3CA alterations confirmed by ctDNA or tissue.
outcome: Investigator-assessed PFS
safety_summary: Hyperglycemia (G3+ ~6%), stomatitis (G3+ ~6%), diarrhea (G3+ ~4%), rash. Discontinuation due to AE ~6.5%.
notes: Cross-tumor anchor for inavolisib's PIK3CA-mutant pharmacology — drove the Oct 2024 FDA approval in HR+/HER2- breast cancer. INTRINSIC mCRC platform (NCT04929223) extends inavolisib + bev into PIK3CA-mut mCRC; cross-tumor activity here is the strongest mechanistic basis.

intervention_label: Regular aspirin use in PIK3CA-mutant CRC (Nurses' Health + Health Professionals cohorts)
intervention_dose: Regular aspirin use (≥325 mg/week, self-reported)
indication: Resected colorectal cancer stratified by tumor PIK3CA mutation
population_detail: 964 stage I-IV CRC patients from NHS + HPFS; tumor PIK3CA mutation status assessed retrospectively; 17% PIK3CA-mut.
comparator: Non-regular aspirin users within each PIK3CA stratum
outcome: CRC-specific and overall mortality by aspirin use × PIK3CA status
safety_summary: Aspirin GI-bleed / ulcer risk class-typical; not formally captured in this cohort analysis.
notes: Foundational observational signal that aspirin halves CRC-specific mortality in PIK3CA-mut patients. The patient's metastatic setting differs from the resected adjuvant cohort here, but the biomarker direction matches.

intervention_label: Adjuvant low-dose aspirin in PI3K-pathway-altered resected CRC (ALASCCA)
intervention_dose: Aspirin 160 mg PO QD for 3 years
indication: Resected stage I-III rectal or stage II-III colon cancer with somatic PI3K-pathway alteration (PIK3CA / PIK3R1 / PTEN)
population_detail: n=626 randomized; 1,103 of 2,980 screened (37%) carried a PI3K-pathway alteration. Group A = PIK3CA exon 9/20 mut; Group B = other PI3K-pathway alterations.
outcome: Time to recurrence at 3 years
safety_summary: Aspirin G3+ bleeding events ~3% vs ~2% placebo; tolerability acceptable, with no excess in serious AEs driving discontinuation.
notes: Practice-changing 2025 phase 3 — first prospective biomarker-driven aspirin RCT in CRC to meet its primary endpoint. The patient's PIK3CA M1043I (kinase-domain, exon 20) would fall in Group A. Decision-relevant for post-HIPEC adjuvant-equivalent maintenance discussion; metastatic context limits direct extrapolation, but mechanism rationale and class safety are well-mapped.

intervention_label: Adjuvant celecoxib in PIK3CA-activated stage III colon cancer (CALGB/SWOG 80702)
intervention_dose: Celecoxib 400 mg PO QD for 3 years (added to FOLFOX 3 vs 6 months)
indication: Resected stage III colon cancer, PIK3CA-activating subset
population_detail: Pre-specified biomarker subgroup of CALGB/SWOG 80702 (n=2,524 randomized total; ~16% PIK3CA-activating).
design: Pre-specified biomarker subgroup of randomized double-blind phase 3
outcome: DFS and OS in PIK3CA-activating subset
safety_summary: Celecoxib G3+ AEs class-typical (cardiovascular, GI). Cohort safety dominated by FOLFOX backbone toxicity.
notes: Pre-specified PIK3CA-activating subset of CALGB/SWOG 80702 — 56% DFS HR and 41% OS HR favoring celecoxib are large effects, despite the overall trial being negative. Mechanism parallels the aspirin signal (COX-2 → PGE2 → PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis). Decision-relevant for combination strategy with the patient's PIK3CA M1043I.

intervention_label: Eprenetapopt (APR-246) phase 1 in TP53-mutant solid tumors and hematologic malignancies
intervention_dose: APR-246 IV escalation (50-90 mg/kg/day × 4 days); RP2D 67 mg/kg/day
indication: Solid tumors and hematologic malignancies with TP53 mutation
population_detail: n=22, mixed solid + heme; first-in-human PK and tolerability study.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, biological activity (p53 reactivation by transcriptional readout)
variance_or_ci: no DLTs to top dose; PD activity by gene-expression panel
safety_summary: Fatigue, nausea, dizziness, confusion most common. No DLTs at RP2D. Reversible neuropsychiatric effects (confusion, dizziness) at higher doses limited further escalation.
notes: Lehmann/Mohell phase 1 — first APR-246 readout established the agent's tolerability and biological activity but did not establish solid-tumor efficacy. Aprea pivoted to MDS/AML, then failed phase 3 in TP53-mut MDS (2020). The TP53-mut solid-tumor combination studies (NCT04383938 APR-246 + pembrolizumab) ran without clear positive signal.

intervention_label: Eprenetapopt + pembrolizumab phase 1b in TP53-mutant advanced solid tumors
intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 4.5 g IV QD ×4 + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W
indication: Advanced solid tumors with TP53 mutation
population_detail: n=24, mixed TP53-mut solid tumors (NSCLC, urothelial, gastric, prostate, others). TP53 mutations spanned hotspots and non-hotspots; specific R273 subset not separately analyzed.
outcome: Safety and ORR
variance_or_ci: 2 PRs in 24 evaluable
safety_summary: Combination tolerated; G3+ fatigue, ataxia, encephalopathy reported. No new pembrolizumab safety signals.
notes: Modest single-arm signal in TP53-mut solid tumors; not enough to support routine use in TP53 R273 mCRC. The Aprea program effectively closed after the company pivoted away from solid tumors. R273-specific pharmacology is not addressed.

exclusion_reason: Rezatapopt (PC14586, PYNNACLE) is a Y220C-pocket-specific p53 reactivator. The patient's TP53 R273 has a different structural pathology (DNA-binding domain hotspot, not the Y220C pocket); rezatapopt does not target R273. PMV's program is allele-specific by design.
intervention_label: Rezatapopt (PC14586, PYNNACLE) in TP53 Y220C solid tumors
notes: Y220C-only program; R273 patient not biomarker-eligible. Listed so the board sees Y220C-targeted reactivator pharmacology exists but is allele-specific.

intervention_label: Navitoclax (ABT-263) + irinotecan phase 1 in solid tumors
intervention_dose: Navitoclax 150 mg PO QD + irinotecan 75 mg/m2 weekly (RP2D)
indication: Advanced solid tumors (mixed; CRC subset present)
population_detail: n=39 advanced solid tumors. UGT1A1*28 7/7 homozygotes excluded by amendment due to G3+ diarrhea / febrile neutropenia signal.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, anti-tumor activity
variance_or_ci: RP2D defined; PR in 1 patient each schedule
safety_summary: Thrombocytopenia (dose-dependent, on-target BCL-xL), diarrhea (irinotecan), neutropenia. Combination tolerable at RP2D but on-target platelet toxicity is the key class issue.
notes: Most directly applicable precedent for the patient's BCL2L1 (BCL-xL) + TOP1 co-amplification biology — navitoclax + irinotecan was tolerable at the published RP2D, with on-target thrombocytopenia driving the field's move to DT2216 PROTACs. Modest activity (5% ORR overall) in unselected solid tumors; selection for BCL2L1-amp tumors was not tested.

intervention_label: Navitoclax (ABT-263) monotherapy phase 1 in SCLC and other solid tumors
intervention_dose: Navitoclax PO 10-475 mg QD (continuous, 14-of-21, or 7-of-21 schedules)
indication: Small-cell lung cancer and other advanced solid tumors
population_detail: n=47 (SCLC predominant); other solid tumors included.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, ORR
variance_or_ci: 1 PR in SCLC; SD in additional patients
safety_summary: Class-defining on-target thrombocytopenia (BCL-xL on platelets). DLT was thrombocytopenia; RP2D required platelet-protective lead-in dosing.
notes: Foundational navitoclax monotherapy paper — establishes the class-defining platelet toxicity that motivated DT2216 PROTAC design. CRC subset not separately analyzed.

intervention_label: DT2216 BCL-xL PROTAC phase 1 first-in-human in r/r solid tumors
intervention_dose: DT2216 IV escalation; RP2D 0.4 mg/kg IV biweekly
indication: Relapsed/refractory advanced solid tumors
population_detail: n=20 heavily pre-treated solid tumors (mixed histologies). Median age 60.5; 60% female.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, PK, target engagement (BCL-xL degradation in peripheral leukocytes)
variance_or_ci: transient thrombocytopenia resolving in 3-4 days; RP2D 0.4 mg/kg IV BIW

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: stable disease only; no objective responses

outcomes.name: AE_rate
outcomes.notes: platelet-sparing relative to navitoclax via PROTAC selectivity

safety_summary: Asymptomatic rapid-recovery thrombocytopenia (cycle 1 only); no major bleeding. RP2D 0.4 mg/kg IV BIW. Class-leading platelet sparing vs navitoclax.
notes: First-in-human DT2216 readout — establishes platelet-sparing profile and target engagement. No CRC-specific cohort; SD only as monotherapy. Combination cohorts (DT2216 + paclitaxel ovarian; DT2216 + irinotecan pediatric) are the relevant forward steps for the patient's BCL2L1/TOP1 amp biology. PMC12613848.

intervention_label: AZD0466 dual BCL-2/BCL-xL inhibitor (dendrimer-conjugated AZD4320) phase 1
intervention_dose: AZD0466 IV per dose-escalation; multiple cohorts (low / intermediate / high TLS risk)
indication: Advanced hematologic malignancies and solid tumors at varying TLS risk
population_detail: Phase 1 dose-escalation across hematologic malignancies (NHL, MM) and solid-tumor low-TLS-risk cohort. Solid-tumor expansion limited.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, PK
variance_or_ci: no DLTs reported in abstract; dose-escalation ongoing
safety_summary: Dendrimer conjugation mitigates the cardiovascular signal of free AZD4320. No DLTs in early dose-escalation per abstract; on-target thrombocytopenia monitored.
notes: Abstract-only AACR 2024 readout — full safety / activity table not yet published. Mechanism rationale for BCL2L1-amp tumors is mixed because AZD0466 is dual Bcl-2/Bcl-xL rather than BCL-xL-selective. Audit-trail row for the BCL-xL class landscape. AE detail not in abstract; full toxicity table not in PMC; no published manuscript yet.

intervention_label: Pelcitoclax (APG-1252) dual Bcl-2/Bcl-xL inhibitor phase 1
intervention_dose: APG-1252 IV per dose-escalation
indication: SCLC and other solid tumors
population_detail: Mixed solid tumors, SCLC-enriched cohort.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, anti-tumor activity
variance_or_ci: few PRs; thrombocytopenia dose-limiting
safety_summary: On-target dose-limiting thrombocytopenia, similar to navitoclax. Program has slowed since 2023.
notes: Limited published data; Ascentage program has decelerated post-2023. Audit-trail row for BCL-xL class. AE detail incomplete in available abstracts.

intervention_label: Botensilimab + balstilimab phase 1 in r/r MSS mCRC
intervention_dose: Botensilimab 1 or 2 mg/kg IV Q6W + balstilimab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W
indication: Relapsed/refractory MSS metastatic colorectal cancer
population_detail: n=101 r/r MSS mCRC, mixed liver / non-liver metastatic distribution. Most patients had ≥3 prior lines.
outcome: Confirmed ORR, mOS, mPFS by liver-metastasis status
variance_or_ci: 95% CI 10-26%; NLM subset ORR 22%, LM subset ORR 5%
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR not reached (NLM subset); mOS 20.9 mo (NLM)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: primary efficacy signal in patients without active liver mets

safety_summary: Immune-mediated AEs (diarrhea/colitis, hepatitis, rash) characteristic of Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 + PD-1. G3+ irAE ~35%; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Most decision-relevant MSS-CRC ICI signal in the modern era — Fc-enhanced CTLA-4 (botensilimab) + PD-1 (balstilimab) delivered a real signal in MSS mCRC, especially in no-liver-mets patients. The patient's peritoneal-only disease post-liver-met resection is the NLM phenotype. Strongest MSS-CRC immunotherapy candidate at 2L+. PMC11405281.

intervention_label: Botensilimab ± balstilimab in MSS mCRC NLM (randomized phase 2 update)
intervention_dose: Botensilimab 75 mg IV Q6W + balstilimab 240 mg IV Q3W (selected RP3D)
indication: Refractory MSS metastatic colorectal cancer without active liver metastases
population_detail: n=123 MSS mCRC NLM, randomized to BOT mono vs BOT+BAL. Peritoneum, soft-tissue, and brain metastases all responded.
journal: J Clin Oncol (ASCO GI / ESMO GI 2024 abstracts)
outcome: ORR, mOS, peritoneal-site response
variance_or_ci: BOT+BAL ORR 19% confirmed; BOT mono lower

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: ESMO GI 2024 update; median approaching 2 years

safety_summary: Combination irAE profile consistent with phase 1 — diarrhea/colitis, hepatitis, pyrexia. Discontinuation due to irAE manageable; no treatment-related deaths reported in updates.
notes: ASCO GI 2025 / ESMO GI 2024 randomized phase 2 update — peritoneal-site response specifically called out, which is the patient's dominant disease compartment. CCTG phase 3 (NCT07152821, in trials.jsonl) is the next confirmatory step. Strongest current MSS-CRC ICI-combo signal. Toxicity rates from ASCO abstract; full per-term breakdown pending peer-reviewed publication.

exclusion_reason: REGONIVO regorafenib + nivolumab in MSS gastric/CRC. Anti-angiogenic + anti-PD-1 backbone — mechanism does not target the patient's nominated features. Listed in audit trail as the foundational MSS-CRC ICI-combination signal (later largely failed to replicate in Western cohorts).
intervention_label: Regorafenib + nivolumab (REGONIVO, EPOC1603) MSS gastric/CRC
notes: Japanese phase 1b: ORR 36% in MSS CRC (n=25). Western replication studies (Fakih 2021, eClinicalMedicine 2023) failed to confirm. Audit-trail row for MSS-CRC ICI landscape.

exclusion_reason: Atezolizumab ± cobimetinib vs regorafenib in 3L+ mCRC (mostly MSS). Negative phase 3 — ICI + MEK inhibition does not target the patient's nominated features.
intervention_label: Atezolizumab ± cobimetinib vs regorafenib (IMblaze370, 3L+ mCRC)
notes: Negative: mOS 8.87 (atezo+cobi) vs 7.10 (atezo) vs 8.51 (regorafenib) mo. Reinforces that MAPK + PD-L1 blockade is insufficient for immune-excluded MSS CRC.

exclusion_reason: Pembrolizumab in MMR-deficient solid tumors (Le 2015). Patient is MSS / TMB-low / PD-L1-neg by intake — the opposite of the Le 2015 responder phenotype. Listed for completeness because this paper anchors the MSI-H exception that the patient does NOT have.
intervention_label: Pembrolizumab in MMR-deficient mCRC (Le et al.)
notes: Landmark dMMR / pMMR contrast — ORR 40% (dMMR CRC) vs 0% (pMMR CRC). Defines why MSS-CRC remains ICI-cold.

exclusion_reason: Nivolumab + ipilimumab in dMMR/MSI-H mCRC (CheckMate 142). Patient is MSS — out of biomarker scope.
intervention_label: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (CheckMate 142, MSI-H mCRC)
notes: MSI-H only; ORR 55% (4-yr update 65%). Audit-trail row defining the MSI-H exception.

intervention_label: Galunisertib (TGFbR1 SMI) + nivolumab phase 1b/2 in solid tumors and NSCLC
intervention_dose: Galunisertib 50 mg QD-150 mg BID + nivolumab 3 mg/kg Q2W
indication: Advanced refractory solid tumors and recurrent NSCLC, hepatocellular carcinoma
population_detail: n=75 across phase 1b dose-escalation and phase 2 expansion. Mixed tumor types — solid-tumor cohort included CRC.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, ORR
variance_or_ci: PRs in NSCLC and HCC cohorts; CRC subset without confirmed responses
safety_summary: Galunisertib + nivolumab combination tolerated. No DLTs; class-typical TGFb-axis cardiovascular signal monitored.
notes: Closest TGFb-axis + ICI clinical readout. No CRC-specific responder signal; SMAD4-loss-stratified analysis not performed. Galunisertib program subsequently wound down at Lilly. Cross-tumor proof of tolerability only.

intervention_label: SMAD4 expression loss as prognostic biomarker in colon cancer
intervention_dose: Observational biomarker (no intervention)
indication: Resected colon cancer (stage I-III predominant)
population_detail: n=1,170 colon cancer specimens, SMAD4 IHC, multivariable Cox adjustment for stage, differentiation, adjuvant therapy, lymphovascular invasion.
outcome: 5-year PFS and 7-year CSS by SMAD4 expression
safety_summary: Not applicable.
notes: Independently prognostic SMAD4 loss in colon cancer after adjustment for stage and other covariates. Supports the SMAD4 R361H pessimistic-prognostic framing for the patient and the rationale for trial enrichment around TGFb-axis modulation. PMC6755646.

intervention_label: ST316 (beta-catenin/BCL9 disruptor) phase 1 in Wnt/beta-catenin-driven solid tumors
intervention_dose: ST316 IV per dose-escalation (phase 1)
indication: Advanced solid tumors with Wnt/beta-catenin pathway alterations (APC, CTNNB1, AXIN1)
population_detail: Phase 1 dose-escalation enrolled solid tumors likely to harbor Wnt-pathway abnormalities — CRC subset prominent.
outcome: Safety, PK, target engagement (nuclear-to-cytoplasm beta-catenin shift), preliminary activity
variance_or_ci: SD as primary efficacy signal; no ORR yet
safety_summary: Safe and well tolerated across doses; no DLTs reported at presented doses. AE detail abstract-only.
notes: ASCO GI 2025 abstract — ST316 is the most directly Wnt-axis-targeted asset in active CRC trials. APC E1295 (patient) sits in the mutation cluster region; mechanism rationale is direct. Phase 2 CRC expansion (NCT05848739) includes FOLFIRI-bev and TAS-102-bev arms aligned with the patient's likely sequence. Abstract-only; full toxicity table not yet published.

intervention_label: WNT974 (LGK974) porcupine inhibitor phase 1 in advanced solid tumors
intervention_dose: WNT974 5-30 mg PO QD; RP2D 10 mg QD
indication: Advanced solid tumors, biomarker-unselected (Wnt pathway hypothesis)
population_detail: n=94 advanced solid tumors. AXIN2 expression by RT-PCR used as PD biomarker.
outcome: Safety, RP2D, target engagement (AXIN2 reduction), ORR
variance_or_ci: no ORs by RECIST 1.1; SD 16%, mDoR ~20 wks

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.effect_size: AXIN2 reduction in 94% skin biopsies, 74% tumor biopsies

safety_summary: Dysgeusia (50%) reflects on-target Wnt inhibition. Bone loss / fragility signals (osteopenia) emerged as a class concern.
notes: Foundational porcupine-inhibitor readout — pharmacologically active on Wnt but no objective responses, supporting the field-wide skepticism that 'just inhibit Wnt secretion' is insufficient for APC-mutant CRC. APC-loss tumors are RNF43-fusion-naive and likely resistant to porcupine inhibition. Audit-trail row anchoring the Wnt-class evidence base.

intervention_label: Capivasertib (AZD5363) phase 2 in AKT1 E17K-mutant solid tumors
intervention_dose: Capivasertib 480 mg PO BID (4-on / 3-off)
indication: Solid tumors with AKT1 E17K mutation
population_detail: n=58 AKT1 E17K solid tumors (ER+ breast, gynecologic, other; CRC ~10%).
outcome: ORR / PFS by tumor type
variance_or_ci: mPFS 5.5 mo (ER+ breast); 6.6 mo (gyn); 4.2 mo (other)
safety_summary: Hyperglycemia, rash, diarrhea, stomatitis class-typical for AKT inhibition. G3+ hyperglycemia ~24%.
notes: Cross-tumor anchor for capivasertib in AKT-mutant solid tumors — not PIK3CA-specific. Closest published data on capivasertib activity in non-breast solid tumors. The CAPItello-292 / CAPItello-291 CRC + PIK3CA-axis data have not posted as of 2026. Audit-trail row for the AKT-inhibitor class option.

intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), oral pan-RAS(ON) multi-selective inhibitor, in RAS-mutated PDAC
intervention_dose: Daraxonrasib 300 mg PO QD (efficacy dose); safety pooled across doses up to 300 mg
indication: Previously treated advanced RAS-mutated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
population_detail: RAS-mutant PDAC; efficacy anchored to the 300 mg second-line RAS G12 subset (n=26) and the G12/G13/Q61 subset (n=38). Codons 12/13/61 only — no A59 alleles enrolled.
outcome: ORR in second-line RAS G12 PDAC
safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs in 30% at doses up to 300 mg; characteristic on-target MAPK toxicities were rash, stomatitis/mucositis, and diarrhea, with nausea, vomiting, and fatigue.
notes: Registrational pivotal dataset for the pan-RAS(ON) mechanism, but in PDAC on codon-12/13/61 alleles, not CRC and not A59T. Read as cross-tumor mechanistic precedent for reaching the patient's switch-II KRAS A59T; direct A59T efficacy is unproven.

intervention_label: Daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy in RAS-mutant colorectal cancer (RMC-6236-001 CRC cohort)
intervention_dose: Daraxonrasib 300 mg PO QD
indication: Advanced RAS-mutant colorectal cancer, heavily pretreated
population_detail: RAS-mutant CRC dose-escalation/expansion subset of RMC-6236-001. Data-cutoff 30 Sep 2024. Enrolled alleles are codon 12/13/61 per protocol; the CRC signal is not A59T-specific.
design: Phase 1/2 single-arm, CRC subset of a multi-tumor basket
outcome: ORR in RAS-mutant CRC
notes: Corporate clinical update, not peer-reviewed; CRC-specific N and CIs not disclosed. The CRC monotherapy ORR (9%) runs well below the PDAC figures, which tempers the pan-RAS-in-CRC expectation. AE breakdown not reported at cohort level, so toxicities left empty; the pooled safety sits on the Wolpin NEJM row for this intervention.

intervention_label: Discovery of daraxonrasib (RMC-6236): codon-agnostic RAS(ON) tri-complex mechanism
indication: Preclinical characterization of a pan-RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor across RAS variants
population_detail: Cell-line and structural work spanning wild-type KRAS and G12V/G12C/G12D/G12R/G13D/Q61X. The compound occupies a CypA-SWI/SWII composite pocket and leaves the G12/G13/Q61 groove unoccupied, the structural basis for binding mutant and wild-type RAS with similar affinity.
design: Preclinical med-chem and structural biology (drug-discovery report)
outcome: Codon-agnostic RAS binding and pERK suppression
notes: The mechanistic anchor for why a pan-RAS(ON) drug could reach a non-canonical switch-II A59T: it binds outside the mutated codon groove and engages SWI/SWII rather than the mutant residue. A59T was not tested here, so this supports the rationale without demonstrating A59T activity.

intervention_label: Darlifarnib (KO-2806, farnesyltransferase inhibitor) + adagrasib in KRAS G12C solid tumors (FIT-001)
intervention_dose: Darlifarnib 3-5 mg PO + adagrasib (standard dose)
indication: KRAS G12C-mutated advanced solid tumors (NSCLC, PDAC, CRC)
population_detail: 26 response-evaluable KRAS G12C patients; 43% had >=3 prior lines. CRC ORR quoted for the KRAS-inhibitor-naive subset. The clinical combination is G12C-restricted via adagrasib, not A59T.
outcome: Confirmed ORR in CRC (KRAS-inhibitor-naive)
safety_summary: Reported as a manageable safety profile for the 3-5 mg darlifarnib + adagrasib combination; per-term grade 3+ AE breakdown not in the abstract.
notes: ASCO 2026 abstract; not PubMed-indexed, so PMID null. FTI mechanism (blocking RAS prenylation downstream of the mutated codon) is the codon-agnostic rationale for A59T, but every enrolled CRC patient carried G12C and received G12C-selective adagrasib, so this is not A59T evidence. Per-term toxicities absent from the abstract; toxicities left empty.

intervention_label: Darlifarnib (KO-2806) resensitizes RAS-inhibitor-relapsed tumors (preclinical)
indication: Preclinical RAS/RAF-driven tumor models relapsing on RAS-pathway inhibition
population_detail: Cell-line and xenograft models; FTI added to RAS inhibition to counter adaptive/innate resistance. Not allele-restricted to canonical codons in the mechanistic work.
design: Preclinical in vitro / in vivo pharmacology
outcome: Resensitization to RAS inhibition
effect_size: restored tumor-growth inhibition on FTI + RAS inhibitor
notes: Supports the darlifarnib + pan-RAS combination logic that the FIT-001 program is testing. Preclinical only and not A59T-specific; relevant to the case as the resistance-management rationale behind pairing an FTI with a pan-RAS agent.

intervention_label: NST-628, brain-penetrant pan-RAF/MEK nondegrading molecular glue (preclinical)
indication: Preclinical RAS- and RAF-driven solid-tumor models
population_detail: Cell-line and xenograft models across RAS- and RAF-driven cancers; NST-628 stabilizes inactive RAF-MEK complexes to block ERK signaling downstream of RAS, so activity does not depend on the specific upstream KRAS codon.
outcome: RAS-MAPK pathway suppression across RAS/RAF variants
effect_size: ERK-pathway suppression across diverse RAS/RAF drivers
notes: Mechanistic basis for reaching A59T by acting at RAF/MEK below the RAS node. First clinical readout (NCT06326411) came at AACR 2026 as a corporate update: 38% response and 85% DCR in NRAS/BRAF class II/III melanoma, no CRC or A59T data yet, so the clinical signal is not captured as a separate row.

intervention_label: RLY-2608 (mutant-selective allosteric PI3K-alpha inhibitor) + fulvestrant, PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer (ReDiscover)
intervention_dose: RLY-2608 (RP2D per ReDiscover) + fulvestrant 500 mg IM
indication: PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer
population_detail: Response-evaluable n=31; the kinase-domain PIK3CA subgroup is the on-point comparator for the patient's kinase-domain M1043I. Breast cancer, not CRC.
outcome: ORR in kinase-domain PIK3CA subgroup
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AEs in ~36%; hyperglycemia any-grade ~52% but mostly grade 1 (grade 3 ~3%), with markedly less rash, diarrhea, and stomatitis than wild-type-sparing-poor PI3K inhibitors. Discontinuation for AEs ~2%.
notes: ASCO 2025 abstract; not PubMed-indexed, PMID null. The kinase-domain PIK3CA subgroup is the reason this is decision-relevant for M1043I, but the population is breast cancer plus fulvestrant, so it is off-tumor precedent. Predictive confidence for a rarer kinase-domain allele like M1043I is lower than for canonical H1047R. Discovery/proof-of-concept for RLY-2608 is Varkaris et al., Cancer Discov 2024 (PMID 37916956; DOI 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-23-0944).

intervention_label: Tersolisib (STX-478), oral mutant-selective allosteric PI3K-alpha inhibitor, first-in-human
intervention_dose: STX-478 20-160 mg PO QD; MTD/RP2D 100 mg QD
indication: PIK3CA-mutant advanced solid tumors (HR+/HER2- breast, gynecologic, other)
population_detail: 61 treated (29 HR+/HER2- breast, 32 other solid tumors); 43 response-evaluable. Kinase-domain and helical-domain PIK3CA alleles both enrolled, with activity independent of domain. No CRC-specific efficacy broken out.
outcome: ORR across tumor types
safety_summary: Well tolerated to a 100 mg MTD; no grade 3+ wild-type-PI3K-alpha metabolic toxicities (no grade 3+ hyperglycemia, rash, mucositis, or diarrhea). Two grade 3 events (paresthesia) unrelated to PI3K inhibition; fatigue mild-to-moderate.
notes: ESMO 2024 abstract; not PubMed-indexed, PMID null. Directly relevant to M1043I because activity held across kinase- and helical-domain alleles and the wild-type-sparing safety profile eases combination with a RAS-directed agent. Population is breast/gynecologic, not CRC, so off-tumor precedent; predictive confidence for the rarer M1043I allele is lower than for canonical hotspots.

intervention_label: Elironrasib (RMC-6291), RAS(ON) G12C-selective covalent tri-complex inhibitor
exclusion_reason: Mechanism mismatch: elironrasib is G12C-selective (covalent to the G12C cysteine) and cannot engage the patient's switch-II A59T. It appears in the RAS(ON) suite trial NCT07397338 alongside the pan-RAS daraxonrasib, but only the daraxonrasib backbone reaches A59T, so this agent is out of scope for the A59T feature and mirrors the existing G12C-selective rows.

intervention_label: Zoldonrasib (RMC-9805), RAS(ON) G12D-selective tri-complex inhibitor
exclusion_reason: Mechanism mismatch: zoldonrasib is G12D-selective and does not bind the patient's A59T allele. It is part of the RAS(ON) suite trial NCT07397338 but only via the G12D route; the pan-RAS daraxonrasib arm is what carries the A59T rationale, so this codon-restricted agent is out of scope for the case feature.
